title: the 1
subtitle: the sun / the same / the cinema
summary: Use the when there is only one of something, and learn the everyday expressions that take the - and the ones that don't.

lesson.heading: Only one of something
lesson.text: We use **the** when there is only one of something. We also use **the** with a superlative (the best, the oldest ...).

examples.text: Our apartment is on **the tenth floor**.
Buenos Aires is **the capital** of Argentina.
I'm going away at **the end** of this month.

left.label: the - the only one
examples: What's **the best** way to learn a language?

right.label: a/an - one of many
examples: The sun is **a star**. (= one of many stars)
The hotel where we stayed was **a very old hotel**.
We live in **an apartment** on the tenth floor.

lesson.heading: the same
lesson.text: We always say **the same**, never just 'same'.

examples.text: Your sweater is **the same** colour as mine.

lesson.heading: the world, the sun, the sky ...
lesson.text: We say **the world, the universe, the sun, the moon, the earth, the sky, the sea, the ground** and **the country** (= not a town). But we use **Earth** without the when we think of it as a planet, and **space** without the when we mean space in the universe.

examples.text: I love to look at the stars in **the sky**.
Do you live in a town or in **the country**?
**The earth** goes round **the sun**, and **the moon** goes round **the earth**.
There are millions of stars in **space**.
I tried to park my car, but **the space** was too small.

lesson.heading: the cinema, TV, the radio
rows: I go to **the cinema** a lot, but I haven't been to **the theatre** for ages.
I don't listen to **the radio** much.
Can you turn off **the television**, please?
**The internet** has changed the way we live.

lesson.heading: Meals
lesson.text: We usually say **breakfast / lunch / dinner** without the. But when there is an adjective, we say **a big lunch**, **a wonderful dinner**, **an early breakfast**.

examples.text: We had **lunch** in a very nice restaurant.

lesson.heading: Numbered things
lesson.text: We say **size 43, platform 5, room 126, page 29, vitamin A, section B** - without the.

examples.text: Do you have these shoes in **size 43**?

lesson.text: Remember the odd pair: we watch **TV** but we listen to **the radio**.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Our apartment is on the tenth floor. *B:* Is it? I hope there's ___ lift.
exercises.explanation: This is not a specific lift we already know about, so we use a.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Did you have a nice holiday? *B:* Yes, it was ___ best holiday I've ever had.
exercises.explanation: We use the with a superlative: the best holiday.

exercises.prompt: It's a lovely day, isn't it? Yes, there isn't a cloud in ___ sky.
exercises.explanation: There is only one sky, so we say the sky.

exercises.prompt: Would you like to travel in ___ space?
exercises.explanation: Space in the universe takes no article; the space means an empty gap.

exercises.prompt: Yes, I'd love to go to ___ moon.
exercises.explanation: There is only one moon, so we say the moon.

exercises.statement: Sarah spends most of her free time watching the TV.
exercises.explanation: Sarah spends most of her free time watching TV. We say watch TV without the (but turn off the television = the TV set).
We say listen to the radio, even though we say watch TV.

exercises.prompt: It's confusing when two people have ___ name.
exercises.explanation: We always say the same, never just same.

exercises.prompt: This computer is not connected to ___ internet.
The next train to London leaves from ___.
exercises.explanation: Numbered things take no article: platform 3, not the platform 3.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: You'll find the information you need at the top of page 15.
exercises.explanation: the information (we know which information) and the top (there is only one top), but page 15 with no article.

exercises.prompt: Which of these expressions take the, and which take no word at all?
